I went through both. The one that feels more natural to me is the picker version. When I open it, it shows me the labels I already have so I can just check the ones I want, and there's still a spot to type a brand-new one — I made "Weekend plans" that way and the card ended up showing both "Recipes" and "Weekend plans" like it should.

The reason I prefer that over the plain type-it-in version is important to me: if I have to type every label fresh from memory, I'll eventually fumble one — type "recipe" when I already have "Recipes" — and end up with two labels that mean the same thing scattered across my collection. Seeing my existing labels offered to me as I go is what keeps that tidy. So whichever way we build it, I'd want it to surface the labels I already have when I'm labeling something, not just make me retype them blind. The picker does that naturally.

Both versions confirmed the two things I asked about last time — I can make my own labels, and one bookmark can carry more than one. Good.

And yes — I'd definitely want this same labeling control right there when I'm first saving a bookmark, not only when I go back to edit it. Often I know exactly what something is the moment I save it, and I'd want to file it away then and there.
